newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania amends law on greenfield investments.
newsitem.headline: Romania amends law on greenfield investments.

text.p: Romania rolled out a red carpet for greenfield investments on Monday when foreign investment incentives, including cuts in import duties and tax reductions, came into force.
"The new legislation is, in principle, one more step forward to consolidate a proper framework for foreign investment in this country," a Western analyst said.

Under a bill published in the Official Gazette on Monday, the new incentives are granted to firms with a starting capital of at least $350,000, compared to a previous figure of $50 million, and whose capital is at least 20 percent foreign.
"I think the new bill brings the figures to more realistic levels and the message is out for foreign investors to come," said a second analyst.
The new regulations, which amend a 1991 law on foreign investment, are part of an ambitious reform programme launched by the new centrist government.
Total direct foreign investments in the Balkan country since the 1989 overthrow of communist rule amount to little over $2.5 billion.
"The business climate is positive and the new bill helps establish a clear and understandable legal framework, which is a good step," one analyst said.
Under the new law, exemptions from import duties are granted for all machinery, equipment, means of transport and installations needed to launch the investment in Romania.

A company with fully or partially foreign owned capital benefits from a 50 percent cut in customs duties for imports of raw materials, machinery and spare parts in the first two years of activity or for up to four years after it was registered with the Commercial Register, the new bill said.

Under the new rules, tax on profit paid by companies with a minimum 20 percent foreign participation would amount to 15 percent in the first two years of operation, compared with the current 38 percent.

Companies with a starting cash capital larger than $5 million would have the ceiling of 15 percent tax on profit extended for up to five years of activity. They would also benefit from the 50 percent cut in import taxes for raw materials and spare parts for an additional three years.

The bill also said facilities would be granted to companies which promote exports of their products, invest in infrastructure, tourism and environment protection or re-invest at least 50 percent of their net profit.
